settings.heading: NMN, NAD⁺ & the biology of aging.
settings.subtext: NAD⁺ isn't a trend — it's one of the most studied molecules in longevity research. Here's what it does, why it declines, and how NMN fits in. With the citations to back it up.

settings.heading: Why levels fall.
settings.lede: Production slows and consumption climbs. By midlife, NAD⁺ can sit at roughly half its youthful level — a shift researchers link to many hallmarks of aging.

settings.title: Precursor in
settings.text: NMN is absorbed and taken up by cells — the direct building block one step from NAD⁺.

settings.title: Conversion
settings.text: The enzyme NMNAT converts NMN into NAD⁺ inside the cell — fast and efficient.

settings.title: Function out
settings.text: Restored NAD⁺ powers energy, sirtuins and repair — the work of cellular maintenance.†
NMN supplementation over weeks significantly increased blood NAD⁺ levels in adults and was well-tolerated.
Long-term oral NMN raised NAD⁺ and mitigated age-associated declines in energy metabolism and insulin sensitivity in mice.
Declining NAD⁺ is implicated across hallmarks of aging; precursors like NMN and NR are leading restoration strategies.
settings.cite: — Covarrubias et al., Nat. Rev. MCB (2021)

settings.text: NMN improved measures of physical performance (walking, fatigue) in middle-aged and older adults in a controlled trial.
Sirtuin activity is NAD⁺-dependent; restoring NAD⁺ reactivates these longevity-associated enzymes.
Human trials to date report NMN is generally safe and well-tolerated at studied doses.

settings.heading: Selected research.
settings.disclaim: † These summaries are educational and simplified. NMN research is ongoing; effects vary by individual, dose and duration. Nothing here is a claim that AEON diagnoses, treats, cures or prevents any disease. Always consult your physician.

settings.heading: The dose is only half the story.
settings.lede: NMN purity varies wildly across the market. A high number on the label means nothing without a test behind it.
